Modern Gene Ontology / pathway-enrichment plots

Source: R/pathways-modern.R
plot_pathways.Rd

Publication-quality replacements for the classic green GO DAG and the horizontal bar plot. Given the output of PathwayAnalysis() (or a single MLP result table) it draws either a dot plot that compares the enriched terms across clusters (the enrichment-map / clusterProfiler::dotplot idiom) or a lollipop plot for a single cluster. Dot area encodes the number of genes in the term and colour encodes \(-\log_{10}\) p on a perceptually-uniform viridis scale.

Usage

plot_pathways(
  pathways,
  style = c("dotplot", "lollipop", "circular"),
  top = 8,
  cluster = NULL,
  source = 1,
  title = NULL,
  palette = "D",
  max_chars = 42,
  wrap = 20,
  cluster_cols = NULL
)

Arguments

pathways

Output of PathwayAnalysis() (a list of sources, each a list of per-cluster results carrying a $Pathways table), a single source's per-cluster list, or a single MLP/data.frame result table.

style

"dotplot" to compare clusters side by side, "lollipop" for one cluster, or "circular" for a radial (sunburst-style) bar plot that groups the terms by cluster around a central hub; bar length encodes \(-\log_{10}\) p, colour encodes the cluster, and each term is a single-line radial label that stays legible as the number of terms grows.

top

Number of top terms (by p-value) to show per cluster.

cluster

For "lollipop" (or to subset a dot plot): which cluster to show, by name (e.g. "Cluster 1") or index. NULL shows all.

source

Which source (index or name) of a full PathwayAnalysis() object to plot. Default 1.

title

Optional plot title.

palette

viridis option passed to ggplot2::scale_colour_viridis_c() ("D" viridis, "C" plasma, "B" inferno, "G" mako, ...).

max_chars

Term descriptions longer than this are wrapped onto two lines for legibility (dot plot / lollipop).

wrap

For style = "circular", the character width at which long term labels are wrapped onto successive lines, so long names stay compact and legible around the ring. Smaller values wrap more aggressively.

cluster_cols

For style = "circular", an optional vector of fill colours for the clusters (cluster bars and legend). Supply the same palette used elsewhere - e.g. the cols passed to Cyclogram() - so the clusters share one colour scheme across figures. Positional by cluster order, or a vector named by cluster. Default NULL uses the package palette.

Value

A ggplot object (invisibly); it is also printed so the function works directly on an open graphics device.

See also

PathwayAnalysis(), PlotPathways()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
P <- PathwayAnalysis(List = L, geneExpr = ge, nrclusters = 3,
                     method = c("limma", "MLP"), geneInfo = geneInfo,
                     geneSetSource = "GOBP", sign = 0.05, niter = 2)
plot_pathways(P, style = "dotplot", top = 8)          # compare clusters
plot_pathways(P, style = "lollipop", cluster = 1)     # one cluster
} # }
